label: Kill verb, me, 'to ...'
summary: German 'to ...' verb that finishes a sentence about the character's signature weapon killing the speaker, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer give 'zu zermalmen', sword or spear 'zu durchbohren', dagger 'auszuweiden'; the axe gives 'niederzustrecken' and is also the fallback. The weapon is read from the character's `signature_weapon` variable. The speaker is the victim (the key names say 'me'). Four game texts use it.

label: Groin kill, me, pronoun
summary: The small German pronoun piece, 'mein', 'mich' or 'mir', that starts a phrase about a groin or waist blow by the signature weapon against the speaker.
details: Mace or hammer give 'mein'; sword, spear and axe give 'mich' (the sword/spear entry is the fallback); dagger gives 'mir'. The matching verb part comes from the DE_2 variant of the same custom loc. The weapon is read from the `signature_weapon` variable.

label: Groin kill clause, me
summary: A whole German clause saying the signature weapon has already wounded the speaker in the groin or waist area, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'mir bereits mein Becken zertrümmert' (smashed my pelvis). Sword or spear (fallback): 'mich bereits vom Hals bis hinunter zum Schritt aufgeschlitzt' (slit me open from neck to crotch). Axe: 'mich bereits im Schritt gespaltet' (split me at the crotch). Dagger: 'mir bereits wiederholt in den Bauch gestochen' (stabbed me repeatedly in the belly). The speaker is the victim. One game text uses it.

label: Groin kill, other, 'to ...'
summary: German phrase pieces about the signature weapon hitting another person's groin or waist, written with her/his or her/him taken from the saved scope `second`.
details: Mace or hammer: her/his pelvis 'zertrümmern'; sword or spear (fallback): 'aufschlitzen' from neck to crotch; axe: 'im Schritt zu spalten'; dagger: stab repeatedly in the belly ('wiederholt in den Bauch stechen'). The pronoun is filled in from `scope:second`, which must be the other person. No game text calls it directly.

label: Groin kill verb, other
summary: A first-person German verb for striking another person's groin or waist with the signature weapon: 'zertrümmere', 'schlitze', 'spalte' or 'steche'.
details: Mace or hammer give 'zertrümmere', sword or spear (fallback) 'schlitze', axe 'spalte', dagger 'steche'. These are bare verbs; the object comes from the DE_2 variant. No game text calls it directly.

label: Jaw or throat clause, me
summary: A German present-tense clause saying the signature weapon hits the speaker's jaw or throat, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'zerschmettert meinen Kiefer' (shatters my jaw). Sword, spear or dagger: 'schlitzt mir die Kehle auf' (slits my throat). Axe, also the fallback: 'durchhackt meine Kehle' (hacks through my throat). The speaker is the victim. One game text uses it.

label: Jaw or throat, other, 'to ...'
summary: German phrase pieces for a blow to another person's jaw or throat, with her/his or her/him taken from the saved scope `second`.
details: Mace or hammer: her/his jaw 'zu zerschmettern'; sword, spear or dagger: the throat 'aufzuschlitzten'; axe (fallback): the throat 'durchzuhacken'. The pronoun is filled in from `scope:second`. No game text calls it directly.

label: Head kill, me, object phrase
summary: A German object phrase for a killing blow by the signature weapon to the speaker's head, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'meinen Schädel zertrümmern' (smash my skull). Sword or spear: 'die Kehle aufschlitzen' (slit the throat). Axe, also the fallback: 'den Kopf abschlagen' (cut off the head). Dagger: 'durchs Auge ins Gehirn stoßen' (thrust through the eye into the brain). One game text uses it.

label: Kill verb, other, 'to ...'
summary: German kill verb after the pronoun for another person (taken from the saved scope `second`), chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: pronoun plus 'zermalmen'; sword or spear: 'durchbohren'; axe (fallback): 'niederstrecken'; dagger: 'ausweiden'. The pronoun is the accusative form for `scope:second`. No game text calls it directly.

label: Kill verb, other, 'I ...'
summary: A first-person German kill verb followed by the pronoun for another person (from the saved scope `second`), chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'zermalme'; sword or spear: 'durchbohre'; axe (fallback): 'strecke'; dagger: 'weide'. For the axe and dagger the rest of the separable verb ('nieder', 'aus') comes from the DE_2 variant. No game text calls it directly.

label: Ribs strike verb, me
summary: A German verb for the signature weapon striking the speaker's ribs: 'gleitet', 'zertrümmert' or 'hackt sich'.
details: Sword, spear or dagger (fallback) give 'gleitet' (glides), mace or hammer 'zertrümmert' (smashes), axe 'hackt sich' (hacks its way). The ribs part ('zwischen meine Rippen' and so on) comes from the DE_2 variant. One game text uses it.

label: Ribs strike verb, other
summary: A first-person German verb for striking another person's ribs with the signature weapon: 'stoße', 'zertrümmere' or 'hacke'.
details: Sword, spear or dagger (fallback) give 'stoße', mace or hammer 'zertrümmere', axe 'hacke'. The ribs part with her/his comes from the DE_2 variant. No game text calls it directly.

label: Breastbone wound, me
summary: A German phrase saying the speaker's breastbone was crushed, severed or broken through by the signature weapon, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'mein Brustbein zerquetscht'. Sword, spear or dagger (fallback): 'mein Brustbein durchtrennt'. Axe: 'mein Brustbein durchschlagen'. One game text uses it.

label: Chest blow clause, me
summary: A German present-tense clause for a blow to the speaker's chest by the signature weapon, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'zerquetscht meine Brust'. Sword, spear or dagger (fallback): 'sticht mitten durch meine Brust'. Axe: 'trifft mich mitten auf der Brust'. One game text uses it.

label: Chest blow, other
summary: German clause ending for a blow to another person's chest, with her/his taken from the saved scope `second`.
details: Mace or hammer: her/his chest 'zerquetscht'. Sword, spear or dagger (fallback): 'durch ... Brust sticht'. Axe: 'Brust trifft'. The pronoun is filled in from `scope:second`. No game text calls it directly.

label: Breastbone verb, other
summary: A first-person German verb plus her/his breastbone (from the saved scope `second`), for a blow by the signature weapon, chosen by weapon type.
details: Mace or hammer: 'zerschmettere'; sword, spear or dagger (fallback): 'durchtrenne'; axe: 'durchschlage'. No game text calls it directly.

label: Weapon part ending, 1
summary: A short German word ending that depends on which part of the signature weapon strikes, chosen by weapon type.
details: Sword, spear and dagger (fallback) give 'e'; mace and hammer give 'er'; axe gives 'er'. The key name suggests the parts point, head and edge, but the game gives only the endings here. One game text uses it.

label: Wound verb particle 1
summary: A small German piece added after a wound verb: ' ein' for a sword or axe, nothing for the other weapons.
details: Sword and axe (fallback) give ' ein'; mace, hammer, spear and dagger give an empty text. One game text uses it.

label: Wound verb particle 2
summary: A small German piece added after a wound verb: ' mit' for a sword or axe, nothing for the other weapons.
details: Sword and axe (fallback) give ' mit'; mace, hammer, spear and dagger give an empty text. The DE_2 variant gives the ending that goes with it. One game text uses it.

label: Thrust verb ending 1
summary: A short German ending for a thrust verb: 'er' for a sword, axe, spear or dagger, 'e' for a mace or hammer.
details: Sword, axe, spear and dagger (fallback) give 'er'; mace and hammer give 'e'. The DE_2 variant gives the verb itself ('versenke' or 'schlage'). Three game texts use it.

label: Weapon ending, 1
summary: A short German ending that goes next to the signature weapon's name so the grammar fits: 'er' for an axe, 'em' for the other weapons.
details: The weapon is the character's `signature_weapon` variable; a sword is the fallback. Vanilla puts it after words such as 'mein' and 'd' in single combat and other events. Variants 1 to 9 share the same conditions and differ only in their text. The game does not say what each number is for.

label: Arm text, 2
summary: A German text that depends on whether the character has the maimed trait: empty if so, 'e' otherwise.
details: A character with the `maimed` trait gets an empty text; everyone else gets 'e' (this is the fallback). Variants 1 to 3 exist; the game does not say what each number is for. One game text uses it.

label: Eye verb, 2
summary: The German verb 'hat' for a one-eyed character, 'haben' for everyone else.
details: A character with the `one_eyed` trait gets 'hat'; everyone else gets 'haben' (the fallback). One game text uses it.

label: Motto 'May God', 2
summary: The German motto opener 'May God', 'May the Perfected', 'May the Divine' or 'May the gods', chosen by the faith of the character's house head.
details: It looks at the last house head of the character's house. Christian, Islamic and Jewish faiths give 'Möge Gott'; Buddhist gives 'Mögen die Vollendeten'; dualist and Zoroastrian give 'Möge das Göttliche'; all other faiths give 'Mögen die Götter'. The last entry (the high god of the faith) can never be chosen, because its trigger is `always = no`, although it is marked as the fallback. Used in one motto text.

label: Grit ending, 2
summary: A German ending for the dirt or debris at the character's location: 'en' on forest or taiga terrain, 'em' elsewhere.
details: Mountains and desert mountains are the fallback. 'en' goes with the twigs of forest and taiga; all other terrains (plains, farmlands, hills, floodplains, desert, oasis, wetlands, jungle, steppe, drylands) give 'em'. The words themselves come from the DE_3, DE_4 and DE_6 variants. One game text uses it.

label: Ground word, 2
summary: A German word for the ground at the character's location, chosen by terrain: dust, dirt, rocks, sand, wet grass, mulch or grass.
details: Farmlands, hills and drylands give 'Dreck'; mountains 'Felsen'; desert mountains 'sandigen Felsen'; desert and oasis 'Sand'; wetlands and floodplains 'nasse Gras'; forest, taiga and jungle 'Mulch'; steppe and plains 'Gras'. 'Staub' (dust) is the fallback; its own trigger asks for a saved `scope:locale` to exist, but as the fallback it is used whenever no terrain matches. Variants 1 to 6 have the same conditions. 28 game texts use this variant.

label: Hand text, 2
summary: The German word 'Hand' for a character with the maimed trait, 'Händen' for everyone else.
details: A character with the `maimed` trait gets 'Hand'; everyone else gets 'Händen' (the fallback). One game text uses it.

label: Mask or face ending, 2
summary: A German ending that depends on whether the character has the disfigured trait: 'e' if so, empty otherwise.
details: A character with the `disfigured` trait gets 'e'; everyone else gets an empty text (the fallback). 17 game texts use this variant.

label: Weapon action piece, 2
summary: A German piece that follows the weapon's name in the single combat intro; empty for most weapons and ' ein' for a spear.
details: Sword (fallback), mace, axe, hammer and dagger give an empty text; spear gives ' ein'. Together with the DE_1 verb ('hebe', 'zücke' ...) it forms the action of readying the weapon. The weapon is read from `signature_weapon`.

label: Heavy blow noun, 2
summary: A German adjective plus noun for a heavy attempted blow with the signature weapon: 'mächtige Hieb', 'Schlag' or 'Stoß'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'mächtige Hieb'; mace and hammer give 'mächtige Schlag'; spear gives 'mächtige Stoß'. Eight game texts use this variant.

label: Heavy blows plural, 2
summary: The plural of the heavy blow phrase: 'mächtigen Hiebe', 'Schläge' or 'Stöße'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'Hiebe'; mace and hammer 'Schläge'; spear 'Stöße', each after 'mächtigen'. Four game texts use this variant.

label: Light blow noun, 2
summary: A German adjective plus noun for a light attempted blow with the signature weapon: 'schneller Schnitt', 'Schwung' or 'Stoß'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'schneller Schnitt'; mace and hammer 'schneller Schwung'; spear 'schneller Stoß'. The heavy version is a separate custom loc. Five game texts use this variant.

label: Light blows plural, 2
summary: The plural of the light blow phrase: 'schneller Schnitte', 'Schwünge' or 'Stöße'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'Schnitte'; mace and hammer 'Schwünge'; spear 'Stöße', each after 'schneller'. Nine game texts use this variant; the single combat text about an unsure attack uses the DE_1 variant of the word.

label: Weapon breaks, 'to ...'
summary: A German 'to ...' verb for how the signature weapon is damaged when it breaks: 'zu verbiegen' (bend) or 'zu spalten' (split).
details: Sword and dagger give 'zu verbiegen'; spear and axe give 'zu spalten'; hammer and mace give 'zu verbiegen'. Two of the entries are marked as fallback. Despite 'past tense' in the key name, the texts are 'zu' infinitives. Three game texts use this variant.

label: Weapon breaks, participle
summary: A German past participle for the broken weapon: 'verbogen' (bent) or 'gespalten' (split).
details: Sword and dagger give 'verbogen'; spear and axe give 'gespalten'; hammer and mace give 'verbogen'. Two entries are marked as fallback. One game text uses it.

label: Weapon breaks, verb form
summary: A German verb form for the weapon breaking: 'verbiegt' (bends) or 'spaltete' (split).
details: Sword and dagger give 'verbiegt'; spear and axe give 'spaltete' (a past form); hammer and mace give 'verbiegt'. Two entries are marked as fallback. The key name says present participle, which does not fit the texts. Two game texts use this variant.

label: Critical blow verb, 2
summary: A German 'to ...' verb for a critical blow with the signature weapon: 'zu schneiden', 'zu zermalmen' or 'zu bohren'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'zu schneiden'; mace and hammer give 'zu zermalmen'; spear gives 'zu bohren'. Three game texts use this variant.

label: Weapon flourish word, 2
summary: A German '-nd' word for how the weapon is moved about: 'wirbelnd' (whirling) or 'fuchtelnd' (flailing).
details: Sword and axe (fallback) give 'wirbelnd'; mace, hammer, dagger and spear give 'fuchtelnd'. Two game texts use this variant.

label: Eye ending, 5
summary: A German ending for a one-eyed character, 'em', or for everyone else, 'en'.
details: A character with the `one_eyed` trait gets 'em'; everyone else gets 'en' (the fallback). Five game texts use it.

label: Grit article, 5
summary: A German article for the dirt or debris at the character's location, chosen by terrain: 'den', 'das' or 'die'.
details: Mountains and desert mountains (fallback), plains, farmlands, hills, floodplains, desert and oasis give 'den'; wetlands, jungle, steppe and drylands give 'das'; forest and taiga give 'die'. Three game texts use it.

label: Ground phrase, 5
summary: A German preposition plus article for the ground at the character's location, chosen by terrain: 'auf den', 'auf die' or 'auf das'.
details: Dust (fallback), dirt, sand and mulch give 'auf den'; rocks and sandy rocks give 'auf die'; wet grass and grass give 'auf das'. Four game texts use it.

label: Mask or face preposition, 5
summary: A German preposition that depends on whether the character has the disfigured trait: 'auf' if so, 'in' otherwise.
details: A character with the `disfigured` trait gets 'auf'; everyone else gets 'in' (the fallback). Two game texts use it.

label: Heavy blows plural, 5
summary: The plural noun for heavy attempted blows: 'Hiebe', 'Schläge' or 'Stöße'.
details: Sword, axe and dagger (fallback) give 'Hiebe'; mace and hammer 'Schläge'; spear 'Stöße'. Four game texts use it.

label: Weapon part ending, 5
summary: A short German ending for the striking part of the weapon: 'e' for sword, spear, dagger or axe, 'en' for mace or hammer.
details: Sword, spear and dagger (fallback) give 'e'; mace and hammer give 'en'; axe gives 'e'. One game text uses it.

label: Weapon ending, 5
summary: A short German ending next to the signature weapon's name: 'er' for an axe, 'es' for the other weapons.
details: Sword (fallback), mace, hammer, spear and dagger give 'es'; axe gives 'er'. Vanilla uses it with the genitive word of DE_6 in the tournament texts.

label: Grit word, 6
summary: A German word for the dirt or debris at the character's location, chosen by terrain, with adjective forms for leaves and grass.
details: Mountains and desert mountains (fallback) give 'Splitt'; plains, farmlands, hills and floodplains 'Dreck'; desert and oasis 'Sand'; wetlands 'Sumpfwasser'; forest and taiga 'Zweige'; jungle 'nasse Laub'; steppe and drylands 'trockene Gras'. Two game texts use it.

label: Ground ending, 6
summary: A German ending for the ground word at the character's location: 'e' on wetlands, floodplains, steppe and plains, 'en' elsewhere.
details: Wet grass and grass give 'e'; dust (fallback), dirt, rocks, sandy rocks, sand and mulch give 'en'. One game text uses it.

label: Mask or face ending, 6
summary: A German ending that depends on whether the character has the disfigured trait: 'e' if so, 'es' otherwise.
details: A character with the `disfigured` trait gets 'e'; everyone else gets 'es' (the fallback). One game text uses it.

label: Weapon name, genitive
summary: The signature weapon's German name in the genitive: 'Schwertes', 'Streitkolbens', 'Axt', 'Hammers', 'Speeres' or 'Dolches'.
details: The weapon is the character's `signature_weapon` variable; a sword is the fallback. This variant gives a full word, not an ending. Vanilla uses it in the tournament texts after the DE_5 ending.

label: Grit article, 7
summary: A German article for the dirt or debris at the character's location, chosen by terrain: 'der', 'das' or 'die'.
details: Mountains and desert mountains (fallback), plains, farmlands, hills, floodplains, desert and oasis give 'der'; wetlands, jungle, steppe and drylands give 'das'; forest and taiga give 'die'. One game text uses it.

label: Mask or face article, 7
summary: A German article that depends on whether the character has the disfigured trait: 'der' if so, 'dem' otherwise.
details: A character with the `disfigured` trait gets 'der'; everyone else gets 'dem' (the fallback). One game text uses it.

label: Weapon ending, 7
summary: A short German ending next to the signature weapon's name: 'e' for an axe, empty for the other weapons.
details: Axe gives 'e'; sword (fallback), mace, hammer, spear and dagger give an empty text. Vanilla uses it after 'ein' or similar words in event texts.

label: Mask or face article, 8
summary: A German article that depends on whether the character has the disfigured trait: 'die' if so, 'das' otherwise.
details: A character with the `disfigured` trait gets 'die'; everyone else gets 'das' (the fallback). Two game texts use it.

label: Weapon article, 8
summary: A German article for the signature weapon: 'der' for an axe, 'dem' for the other weapons.
details: Sword (fallback), mace, hammer, spear and dagger give 'dem'; axe gives 'der'. Vanilla uses it before the weapon's name, for example in the hold court and stress texts.

label: Your weapon word
summary: The German polite 'your' in front of the signature weapon's name: 'Euer' for a sword, 'Eure' for an axe, 'Euren' for the other weapons.
details: Sword (fallback) gives 'Euer'; axe gives 'Eure'; mace, hammer, spear and dagger give 'Euren'. It fits speech addressed to the weapon's owner. The weapon is read from `signature_weapon`.

label: Plural article, A
summary: The German definite plural article 'die' for the form the game labels A.
details: The character's sex picks the entry (is_female = no or yes), but both give 'die'. The game's own comment heading says 'Articles, Definite, Plural'; it does not say what A stands for (probably the accusative case).

label: Plural article, D
summary: The German definite plural article 'der' for the form the game labels D.
details: The character's sex picks the entry, but both give 'der'. German grammar has 'den' for the dative plural and 'der' for the genitive plural, so if D means dative, the D and G labels look swapped. The game does not say what the letters stand for.

label: Plural article, G
summary: The German definite plural article 'den' for the form the game labels G.
details: The character's sex picks the entry, but both give 'den'. If G means genitive, 'den' does not fit German grammar ('der' would), and the D entry holds 'der', so the D and G labels look swapped. The game does not say what the letters stand for.

label: Plural article, N
summary: The German definite plural article 'die' for the form the game labels N.
details: The character's sex picks the entry, but both give 'die'. The game's own comment heading says 'Articles, Definite, Plural'; it does not say what N stands for (probably the nominative case).
